inspiration: Animatronic mascot heads are built from two layers, a static head and a separate jaw sprite, then driven by behaviour components (chomp, spit, swivel, mouth-open). Recreate the layering idea with our own character art.
Table walls drawn as a creature's open jaws (dino top_wall.png, bottom_wall.png, top_wall_tunnel.png) make the boundary part of the monster. Good for zone edges.
A cabinet-mounted machine (Sparky computer) reacts through a sensor behaviour when the ball touches it. Good model for an object that responds to proximity, not only to hits.
The flying-saucer unit runs a state cycle through a cubit (android_spaceship_cubit and state files). A visible multi-state cycle reads well as a timed threat.
Skill-shot and multiball use blink behaviours as telegraphs before a reward. A steady blink cadence tells the player timing without text.
Ball flame trail is a separate effect sprite (packages/pinball_components/assets/images/ball/flame_effect.png). Layer a glow sprite on the moving object for speed read.

briefs.label: Jaw-gate boundary
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A zone edge that is a monster's open mouth makes the wall itself the creature, and the gate can open and close.
briefs.keep: Hinged jaw that opens on a timer; tongue-like ramp; wall silhouette that reads at 375 wide
briefs.change: Make it a different beast (horned gate, not a dino head); use a different palette and jaw count; hinge from the side not the top

briefs.label: Spitting arcade serpent
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A chomp followed by a spit is a readable two-beat attack that turns a bumper into a threat.
briefs.keep: Chomp trigger, short mouth-open telegraph, one projectile out
briefs.change: Different body (armoured slug or plant pod, not a dino); a spore cloud instead of a ball; the attack fires on a timer, not on contact

briefs.label: Cabinet mascot head
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A large head that sits on the cabinet and reacts to ball contact gives the table a face.
briefs.keep: Oversized head that dominates its part of the cabinet; reacts with a short animation to hits
briefs.change: Mechanical face instead of a mascot; asymmetric eyes; different colour ramp and ornament

briefs.label: Telegraphed skill-shot blink
briefs.rule: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
briefs.why: A blink cadence tells the player when a reward is live, with no text needed.
briefs.keep: Steady blink rhythm; reward state visible from across the table
briefs.change: Use a pulse ring or sweeping light instead of a flash; a different count of blinks
